paras: The attempted lynching of Bud Howard was a crowd's pursuit of William ("Bud") Howard, a Black man, through downtown Akron, Ohio, on the night of Saturday, August 11, 1900, after he shot a white man, John Forbes, at the corner of Main and Market streets. According to a wire dispatch, hundreds of men chased Howard shouting "Lynch him!" but he outran them, and police later arrested him in East Akron. Charged with shooting with intent to wound, Howard was moved to the Cleveland jail eleven days later, when a mob seeking another Black prisoner, Louis Peck, besieged Akron's city prison.

Forbes, who lived on Ohio Street, was waiting for a street car at Main and Market with a woman and her daughter when the shooting occurred. The wire called the intersection "the busiest corner in the city." Howard, for his part, claimed that he fired because Forbes had called him "nigger" and had repeatedly insulted him, according to the Akron Daily Democrat.

The Democrat reported that Howard rushed out of the Atlantic Garden, told bystanders to stand aside, and fired a .38-calibre "bull-dog" revolver at Forbes. The bullet lodged in Forbes's leg, where Dr. Harry Todd could not locate it; the wire said he would recover.

In the wire account, a crowd gathered within a minute, and hundreds of men started after Howard yelling "Lynch him!" With a start of a few hundred feet, Howard got away, and the dispatch credited only "the fleetness" of his running with saving him from "a howling mob." He was caught in East Akron, by Officer Eugene Murray according to the Democrat and while boarding a freight train according to the wire. The Democrat's account of his flight and capture does not mention a crowd.

Arraigned in Mayor's court on Monday morning, August 13, Howard pleaded not guilty to shooting with intent to wound; the case was continued to Wednesday and bond was set at $1,000. A number of Black men and women came to court to see him, and "the women cried profusely," the Democrat wrote.

Howard was still in jail on August 22, when a crowd of thousands besieged Akron's city prison in search of Louis Peck, a Black man accused of attempting to assault a six-year-old girl. That afternoon Summit County Sheriff Kelly and Prosecutor Wannamaker took both men to the Cleveland county jail, and one wire described Howard as "accused of a minor offense." In Cleveland, Howard told reporters that he had been jailed before Peck's arrest and that "the Sheriff felt that no colored man would be safe there." On August 27 the Democrat, quoting the Cleveland Leader, reported him still in the county jail and anxious to be tried anywhere but Akron, the last mention of him in the coverage.

The chase reached readers outside Akron through a short wire dispatch printed on August 14 by the Scranton Tribune under "ESCAPED THE MOB" and by the Marietta Daily Leader under "SAVED HIMSELF BY FLIGHT." Both versions called Howard "a negro" and Forbes "a white man," and built the story around the near-lynching rather than the shooting, offering no comment on the crowd. The Akron Daily Democrat, by contrast, ran the shooting as a police-court item under "John Forbes Is Complaining Witness," called Howard "a colored man," and alone printed his reason for firing.

No Black-press report of the chase was found; Howard appears in Black papers only as a passing name in wire coverage of the Peck riot, printed by the Wisconsin Weekly Advocate on August 23 and by the Iowa Bystander on August 24 under "MOB RULES CITY OF AKRON."

The Scranton dispatch placed the shooting "tonight" under an August 13 dateline, while the Marietta version and the Democrat of Monday, August 13, put it on Saturday night; the local paper, which also reported Monday's arraignment, is the stronger evidence. Forbes's wound was in the thigh according to the wire, in one of his legs according to the Democrat, and "in the foot" according to the Cleveland Leader as quoted on August 27. Howard's statement in Cleveland that he had been in jail two months does not match the August 11 date of the shooting.

accounts.label: Wire report
accounts.gist: Howard shot Forbes in an altercation; hundreds chased him yelling "Lynch him!" and only his speed saved him from a "howling mob"; police caught him boarding a freight train.

accounts.label: Local police-court report
accounts.gist: Howard came out of the Atlantic Garden, warned bystanders aside and fired at Forbes, then ran and was caught by Officer Murray; Howard said Forbes had called him "nigger" and repeatedly insulted him. No crowd is mentioned.

accounts.label: Howard's statement in Cleveland
accounts.gist: Howard said he had been jailed before Peck's arrest, that his case had nothing to do with Peck's, and that he was moved because the sheriff felt no colored man would be safe in the Akron jail.

framing.detail: Headlines 'ESCAPED THE MOB' and 'SAVED HIMSELF BY FLIGHT' center the near-lynching, calling Howard 'a Negro' who shot 'a White Man', without comment on the crowd.
The Akron Daily Democrat ran it as police news under 'John Forbes Is Complaining Witness', called Howard 'a colored man', and gave his stated reason for firing.
Later Democrat and wire items mention Howard only as a prisoner moved to Cleveland with Peck, one calling his offense 'minor'.
The Wisconsin Weekly Advocate and Iowa Bystander named Howard only in passing within Peck-riot wire copy; no Black-press account of the chase was found.

conflicts.note: The local Democrat of Monday Aug. 13, which reports a Monday arraignment, places the shooting Saturday night; it is the better evidence.
The local first-day account and wire agree on the leg; the 'foot' version is a later secondhand claim.
